Hi Jenna — great to hear the demo went well.

I'm attaching a short draft blurb (HostedAPI-terms-teaser_v1.docx) that we typically give to procurement for quick intake. It covers the processor role, subprocessors, and where to request the full DPA. A few things to note up-front:
- We treat customer-provided prompt and content as Customer Data; Redwood acts as a data processor for hosted API customers under our DPA.
- We use cloud infra and selected managed services as subprocessors (listed in our subprocessor map in the DPA).
- Cross-border transfers are handled under standard safeguards in the DPA; we can provide SCCs or equivalent on request.

Kimberly is looped in to confirm legal wording is OK for procurement. If you need a 1-line plain-language version instead of a paragraph, say the word and I can shorten.

Kimberly / Vanessa — forwarding NorthStar's procurement request. They want a short, publishable blurb we can put in an intake packet and also paste into vendor questionnaires. Draft is attached.

Request for legal/product review:
- Make sure the blurb doesn't overcommit on residency / transfers. We should avoid promising region-only storage unless customer is on Dedicated/Private.
- Keep the subprocessor line high-level (they want to know "do you use other providers?" not a full list). Provide a link/pointer to subprocessor map + DPA for the detailed list.
- Add a one-line "how to request the DPA" (contact/email/DocuSign).

I've suggested two variants in the doc: a 2–3 sentence paragraph for procurement packets and a one-line plain-language summary for multi-vendor comparisons. Prefer something that legal signs off on verbatim so procurement can paste it.

Thanks — Laura

Laura / Vanessa — thanks for the ping. I reviewed the attached draft and made a concise, procurement-friendly wording below that legal is comfortable with. Key legal clarifications included inline in the attachment (redwood_dpa_snippet.txt).

Suggested 2–3 sentence blurb (for procurement packet):
"Redwood Inference processes customer-submitted content, prompts, and generated outputs as Customer Data and acts as a data processor for hosted API customers under a standard DPA. We engage a limited set of subprocessors (cloud infrastructure and managed services) to operate the service; the current subprocessor list and data transfer safeguards are available in our DPA and subprocessor map. To request a copy of the DPA or SCCs, contact privacy-requests@redwood.com or request via the vendor portal (HubSpot record HS-98765)."

Plain-language one-line summary (for Q&A tables):
"We process customer inputs on your behalf (processor); we use cloud providers as subprocessors — see DPA for details; email privacy-requests@redwood.com for the DPA."

Notes:
- The phrase "acts as a data processor" is important; avoid suggesting control over customer data.
- For cross-border transfer wording, we can say "data transfer safeguards in the DPA" rather than listing SCCs in a short blurb.
- We should avoid naming subprocessor vendors in a short public blurb; those belong in the subprocessor map linked from the DPA.

I've attached the redlined snippet and a clean copy of the blurb. If you want, I can also provide a 1-sentence snippet with an explicit mention of customer controls (deletion/retention) but procurement usually asks for the processor/subprocessor/DPA pointer only.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security | Redwood Inference
